title: an answer carries the scope of its rule: the answer names the scope, the rule carries the same scope, and the journal records it
intent: The wave is the first of the track C of the catch-up plan (the core of the scope of an answer).  The documents of the project named one scope of an approval -- `always` -- and the code had three carriers behind that one name: the rules of the process (the plain answerer), the rules of an attached run and the rules of an ACP session.  A name that covers three carriers is a name that decides nothing: the reader of the code cannot tell what an answer that is remembered "always" actually changed, and the journal of the decision holds no scope at all.  The repair makes the scope a field of its own: the answer names the scope its rule lives in, the rule that the answer writes carries the same scope, and the journal records it.  The canonical dictionary of the scopes is `once`, `run`, `session`, `project`, `global` (the word `run` is added to the four that the documents named, because the code has had the scope of a run all along -- `lib/yeah-run.el:122-123` -- and the documents did not); the kind of the answer stays what it was (`once`/`always`/`reject`) and the scope is a separate field.  The correspondence between a carrier and a scope is written in exactly one place (`yeah-perm--carriers` in `lib/yeah-perm.el`), the dictionary of the kinds of the answer is written in exactly one place (`yeah-approval--reply-kinds` in `lib/yeah-approval.el`), and the surfaces ask the dictionary instead of naming the kinds one by one.  A scope that has no carrier (`project` everywhere, `session` in the attached path) is refused by name with a reason and is never routed silently into the rules of another path.  The lie of the interface is repaired as well: the projection wrote the answer `allow-always` as a refusal (`deny`), and it now writes the true effect `allow` and the scope `session`.  The claim of the wave is new (`an-answer-carries-a-scope`).
objection: The wave repairs the naming of a scope and not the set of the carriers, and the price is named.  (a) **`always` still means three different things**: it writes into the global set of the rules, into the rules of the run and into the rules of the ACP session; the wave *names* the scope that each path corresponds to (`:global`, `:run`, `:session`) and the correspondence lives in one table, but it does not unify the carriers -- that is wave C2.  (b) **The plain answerer is the global path and not the person of the attached path**: an answer given through the shared approval view writes into the rules of the process; which carrier the shared view should carry is a decision of the owner, and the wave names both without deciding.  (c) **The scope `:project` has no carrier**: the vocabulary names it and the check measures that it is refused by name with a reason, but nothing measures what the rules of a project *would* do.  (d) **The journal of the scope has no reader yet**: the field is written (the plain name, one spelling) and the vocabulary of the event accepts it, but no surface of the kernel reads it back.  (e) **The dead hook `yeah-perm-record-decision` stays dead**: its contract has no room for a scope, and reviving it silently is not allowed -- a finding for wave C2 or for the owner.  (f) **The names of the kinds of the answer still appear twice in the kernel**: the dispatch of the approval view is not a second writing of the list, so the check proves "the dictionary is written in one place" and not "the name of a kind appears in one place".  (g) **The scope `:once` and the kind `:once` share a word**: the two dictionaries do not collide, but the word means "this call" in both, and the reader of the journal should know it.  (h) **The layer diagram named four lines that this wave moved** (`lib/yeah-approval-ui.el:114`, `lib/yeah-service-ui.el:413`, `lib/yeah-perm.el:68`, `lib/yeah-approval.el:59`); the diagram is the serialization point of the parent, the parent re-anchored the four numbers and the check of the diagram is green again.
refuted_by: An answer carries no scope, or a scope that is not one of the canonical scopes, or the rule the answer writes carries another scope than the answer, or the journal record of the decision carries no scope, or a scope without a carrier is written into the rules of another path instead of being refused by name, or the dictionary of the answers or of the scopes is written in more than one place.
note: The wave is the first of the three of the track C: the core (C1), the carriers (C2) and the surfaces (C3).  (1) **The nine decisions of the parent are named and dated** (2026-11-21, a rule outside §17.2, the owner may cancel it): the scope is a field of its own and the kind stays the kind; the canonical dictionary of the scopes is `once`, `run`, `session`, `project`, `global`; `always` is not renamed and does not become a synonym of `global`; the scope is written into the journal; on ACP there are new `optionId` and the old `kind`; the names of the kinds are written in one place and the surfaces come to it through a converter; `reject` carries no scope; a scope without a carrier is refused by name with a reason; the control of the claim is a deterministic `sed` that breaks the *writing* of the scope into the rule and not the timing.  (2) **The ground of the decisions is the contradiction of two documents** that the plan of the owner already fixed in section 6: `always` is three different things today, and the prescription of the wave says that `always` is `global` -- that is true for one path only.  (3) **The code and the documents disagreed about the scope of a run**: the code had it (`lib/yeah-run.el:122-123`) and the documents did not name it (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:640` names four scopes); the finding is F46 and the repair of the document is a decision of the owner (section 0 of the plan, D10).  (4) **The proof is a new check of 392 lines with seven stands**, and the seventh stand is the one that repairs the finding F39: the projection of the interface must tell the truth about the answer it writes.  (5) **The controls of the parent were run by the parent** (2026-11-21) on copies of the tree in /tmp, ten controls and no failure: the honest tree of the wave passes the new check (C1a, exit 0); the old tree (the base `1175f91`) with the new check refuses with seventeen of its own assertions (C1b, exit 1); the mutation of the registered control -- a `sed` that breaks the *writing* of the scope into the rule -- refuses with two of its own assertions, "the rule of the session carries the scope nil, not :session" and "the rule of the run carries the scope nil, not :run" (C1c, exit 1), and refuses the same way the two next runs (C1d); the five neighbouring checks of the wave stay green (C1e, exit 0).  (6) **No live run**: no provider, no real client, every measurement is offline, with a fake transport or a fake client.  It is named here and not counted as a success.
